Language index

Every word of the language: keywords, the words that are special inside a form, builtin types, effects, operators and literals, then the AXTAG keys. axiom explain WORD prints the same entry, and hover in your editor shows it.

Words

|>

(|> value (f args...) (g args...))

form

Passes a value through calls from left to right. Each stage receives the preceding result as its first argument; one direct _ places it elsewhere. Every intermediate result is evaluated once. Types, effects and region checks are the same as for ordinary calls.

Reference: reference.md#functions

fn

(fn (name param ...) body)

keyword

Declares a named function at the top level. Its type comes from the (:: name Type) signature above it, and AXTAGs such as ;@axiom:effect(io) go between the two. A function value inside an expression is a lambda; (fn (x) ...) there is refused with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#functions

lambda

(lambda (param ...) body)

keyword

An anonymous function. It captures the bindings it uses, can be passed as a value and may be applied to fewer arguments than it takes, answering another lambda. A lambda with no parameters is refused with AX3068.

Reference: reference.md#lambdas

let

(let name value)

keyword

Declares a local inside a { ... } block. The value is evaluated before the name enters scope; later statements can read it, and a later declaration can shadow it. Use (let mut name value) for a local that set can change. Destructure values with match. The block answers its last expression.

Reference: reference.md#let-bindings

set

(set slot value)

keyword

Overwrites a mut slot. The slot owns what it holds, so the previous value is released (MM-MUT-1). Writing to a binding that is not mut is AX3012.

Reference: reference.md#let-bindings

if

(if test then else)
(if test then)
(if t1 b1 t2 b2 ... else)

keyword

Branches on a Bool. Both branches must have the same type, unless one is (): then the if answers () and the other branch's value is dropped. Leave out the else and the if supplies (), so (if done (println "ok")) needs no filler. With more operands it is a chain: (if t1 b1 t2 b2 else) is (if t1 b1 (if t2 b2 else)). Use braces for a branch of several expressions.

Reference: reference.md#if

match

(match value (pattern body) ... (_ body))

keyword

Compares a value against patterns in order and runs the first body that fits. A pattern is a constructor with binders, a literal, a name or _. A match that misses a constructor is AX3005; a bare capitalised name such as None binds a variable rather than testing a tag, so write (None).

Reference: reference.md#pattern-matching

while

(while test body)

keyword

Repeats the body while the Bool test is true. There is no break or continue: put the stopping condition in the test. The form answers 0.

Reference: reference.md#while-loops

for

(for i in lo..hi body)
(for i in lo..hi by step body)
(for x in vec body)
(for (x i) in vec body)

keyword

Counts over a range, lo included and hi excluded, with an optional by step, or walks a Vec by element or by (x i) element and index. The sequence is evaluated once. A for body is for effects, and the form answers 0.

Reference: reference.md#for-loops

data

(data Name (Ctor Type ...) ...)
(data Name (a) (Ctor a) ...)

keyword

Declares a sum type: a set of constructors, each with zero or more field types. Constructors start with a capital, build values when applied and take values apart in match. Type parameters go in a list after the name.

Reference: reference.md#algebraic-data-types

struct

(struct Name (field : Type) ...)

keyword

Declares a product type with named, typed fields. Build one with named values, (Point :x 1 :y 2), and read a field with a dot, p.x. Supply each field exactly once. Values are evaluated in written order. A field declaration without its : is refused with AX3056.

Reference: reference.md#structs

type

(type Name Type)

keyword

Gives an existing type a second name. Declare parameters between the name and the target, (type Items a (Vec a)), and apply them in type position, (Items Int). Aliases expand transparently and must be finite.

Reference: reference.md#type-aliases

subtype

(subtype Name is Int range lo..hi)

keyword

Declares a range-constrained Int, (subtype Port is Int range 1..65536). A value is checked against the range when it enters the subtype, and a failed check stops the program with its own message.

Reference: reference.md#range-constrained-subtypes

effect

(effect Name (op :: Type) ...)

keyword

Declares an effect: a name and the operations it provides, each with a signature. A call to an operation runs the innermost handle for its effect. A declared effect cannot take a built-in effect's name (AX3054), and an operation needs a type (AX3055).

Reference: reference.md#effects

handle

(handle body (Effect ...) handler)

keyword

Runs a body with a handler installed for an effect's operations. The list names every effect the body performs: a declared effect is intercepted and a built-in one is acknowledged and still reaches the caller. The handler's return value is the operation's result.

Reference: reference.md#effects

region

(region r body)

keyword

Opens a named arena scope. Values allocated inside it are released together when the body ends, and a value that would leave it is refused (AX3059). The compiler infers reference origins through calls and refuses stores into older objects.

Reference: reference.md#regions

parallel

(parallel ((name expr) ...) body)

keyword

Evaluates its bindings at the same time, each on its own task, and runs the body once all of them have answered. A binding may capture a parent value only by borrowing it for the extent of the form (AX3064).

Reference: reference.md#concurrency

macro

(macro (name param ...) template)
(macro name ((name pattern ...) template) ...)

keyword

Declares a macro: a template substituted at its invocation before the type checker runs. The one-rule form names the parameters in the head; the multi-rule form lists patterns and a template for each, which is declarations or one expression, and where the macro is invoked picks which. Hygiene renames the binders a template introduces.

Reference: reference.md#macros

import

(import Module)
(import Module (name ...))

keyword

Brings a module's public names into scope, all of them or the ones listed. A module is a file in the standard library, on AXIOM_PATH or in a dependency. A name declared in two imported modules is AX3014 when used bare.

Reference: reference.md#modules-and-imports

pub

(pub :: name Type)
(pub fn (name ...) body)

keyword

Marks a declaration as public, so other modules can import it. A signature and its function are each marked. A name used from a module that does not export it is AX3023.

Reference: reference.md#modules-and-imports

extern

(extern "crate" (name :: Type (symbol "sym")) ...)

keyword

Binds functions from a Rust crate built by axiom fetch. Each item gives the Axiom type and the symbol it binds; a type that cannot cross the boundary is AX3036. Calling one is an Unsafe operation.

Reference: reference.md#calling-rust

syntax/for

(syntax/for (C (syntax/constructors T)) template)

keyword

Inside a macro template, repeats the template once for each element of a syntax query such as (syntax/constructors T), binding the pattern variable to each.

Reference: reference.md#macros

alloc

(alloc Type)          ; removed

keyword

Removed. The form typed as a pointer and evaluated to 0, so a program holding one held no memory. Allocate with a constructor, a struct or a library function; the compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

begin

(begin a b c)         ; removed: write { a b c }

keyword

Removed. Sequence expressions with a brace block, { a b c }, which answers its last expression. The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

cond

(cond (t1 b1) (t2 b2) else)   ; removed: write (if t1 b1 t2 b2 else)

keyword

Removed. Write the chain with if: (if t1 b1 t2 b2 else) nests as (if t1 b1 (if t2 b2 else)). The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

consume

(consume x)           ; removed

keyword

Removed. It was a parse-time marker that enforced nothing. Ownership follows the memory model's rules without it; the compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

define

(define (name ...) body)     ; removed: write (fn (name ...) body)

keyword

Removed. It was the old spelling of fn, and a language with two spellings of one thing makes every reader learn both. The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

union

(union Name ...)      ; removed: write (data Name ...)

keyword

Removed. An untagged union cannot be pattern-matched safely, since its variants are not distinguishable at run time. Use data; the compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

foreign

(foreign ...)         ; removed: write (extern ...)

keyword

Removed. Bind native code with extern, which names the crate and checks each item's type. The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

trait

(trait Name ...)  (impl Name for Type ...)   ; removed

keyword

Removed. Traits and impls are not part of the language; write the function you want, or derive one with a macro such as deriveEq. The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

impl

(trait Name ...)  (impl Name for Type ...)   ; removed

keyword

Removed. Traits and impls are not part of the language; write the function you want, or derive one with a macro such as deriveEq. The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

emacro

(emacro name rule ...)  ; removed: write (macro name rule ...)

keyword

Removed. It was the multi-rule form for expression templates; macro takes the same rules, (macro total ((total x) x) ((total x rest ...) (+ x (total rest ...)))). The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

cast

(cast Type value)  ; removed: write (as value Type)

keyword

Removed. Write (as value Type), with the value before its target type. Numeric conversions change the number; reference conversions retain their checked ownership and unsafe obligations. The compiler refuses cast with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

mut

(let mut name value)

form

Marks a let binding as a slot that set can overwrite. The slot owns what it holds and releases what set replaces (MM-MUT-1).

Reference: reference.md#mutable-bindings

in

(for x in xs body)

form

Separates the loop variable of a for from the range or Vec it walks.

Reference: reference.md#for-loops

by

(for i in lo..hi by step body)

form

Gives a for over a range its stride. A negative stride counts down; a literal zero stride is refused.

Reference: reference.md#for-loops

is

(subtype Name is Int range lo..hi)

form

In a subtype, names the base type the new type refines.

Reference: reference.md#range-constrained-subtypes

range

(subtype Name is Int range lo..hi)

form

In a subtype, gives the inclusive bounds a value must satisfy.

Reference: reference.md#range-constrained-subtypes

::

(:: name Type)

form

A type signature. At the top level it declares the type of the function or constant below it, (:: bump (-> Int Int)). Inside an effect, it types an operation. Two signatures for one name are refused with AX3006.

Reference: reference.md#functions

->

(-> Arg ... Result)

form

A function type: the argument types, then the result. (-> Int String) takes an Int and answers a String; (-> a a) answers the type it takes.

Reference: reference.md#functions

..

lo..hi

form

A range, lo included and hi excluded in for, both included in a subtype's range.

Reference: reference.md#for-loops

?

(f x)?

form

Propagates a Result or an Option. In a function that answers a Result, (f x)? answers the Ok payload and an Err returns from the function. In a function that answers an Option, it answers the Some payload and None returns from the function. Nothing after the ? runs. This includes a branch, a let body, a loop, a region or a handler. A Result leaves a region only when its payload and its error are both scalars.

Reference: reference.md#propagate-an-error-with-

_

(match v (_ body))
(f _ 2)

form

The wildcard. In a pattern it matches anything and binds nothing. In a call, (f _ 2) builds a lambda over the missing arguments from left to right.

Reference: reference.md#partial-application

as

(as value Type)

form

Converts a value to the written type. Int and Float conversions operate on numeric values; floatToBits and floatFromBits reinterpret bits. A reference converted to a word, such as Int or Foreign, keeps no ownership share: keep the owner alive while using the word. For identity comparisons and hashing, use addrOf. Converting a word to a reference requires effect(unsafe), a valid representation and a live backing owner. A conversion never extends a region's scope.

Reference: reference.md#types

sizeof

(sizeof Type)

form

The size in bytes of a type's representation. Takes exactly one type (AX3069).

Reference: reference.md#types

alignof

(alignof Type)

form

The alignment in bytes of a type's representation. Takes exactly one type (AX3069).

Reference: reference.md#types

asm

(asm (ARCH "template" operand...) ...)

form

Inline assembly: one arm per architecture, each a template and its operands. A form the compiler cannot lower is AX3091, and a template line the assembler rejects is AX3117, reported at that line when the program is built. See the reference's inline assembly section for the operands and options.

Reference: reference.md#inline-assembly

syntax/join

(syntax/join prefix Name)

form

Inside a macro template, builds a name from parts: (syntax/join eq T) with T bound to Colour is eqColour.

Reference: reference.md#macros

syntax/binders

(syntax/binders Ctor x)

form

Inside a macro template, the binder list for a constructor's fields, so a pattern can take any constructor apart without knowing its arity.

Reference: reference.md#macros

syntax/constructors

(syntax/constructors Type)

form

Inside a macro template, the constructors of a data type, answered from the declaration list at expansion time.

Reference: reference.md#macros

syntax/arity

(syntax/arity Ctor)

form

Inside a macro template, how many fields a constructor carries, folded to a literal.

Reference: reference.md#macros

syntax/fields

(syntax/fields Struct)

form

Inside a macro template, the fields of a struct, each as a name and a type.

Reference: reference.md#macros

decl

(decl declaration ...)

form

Inside a declaration macro, splices the declarations it holds into the module.

Reference: reference.md#macros

Int

Int

type

A signed 64-bit integer. Arithmetic wraps. It is also the word a handle or an address is carried in at the raw-memory level, which is why a heap value returned where a signature says Int is refused (AX3004).

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Int8

Int8

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Int16

Int16

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Int32

Int32

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

UInt8

UInt8

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

UInt16

UInt16

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

UInt32

UInt32

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

UInt64

UInt64

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Float

Float

type

An IEEE 754 binary64 number. Convert explicitly with (as value Float) and (as value Int). Numeric types never widen or narrow implicitly. Use floatToBits and floatFromBits to reinterpret bits.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Bool

Bool

type

true or false. The test of if and while, and the result of the comparison and logical operators.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Char

Char

type

A Unicode code point. Utf8 and Str convert between characters and byte strings.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

String

String

type

A byte string. Literals support {name} holes that interpolate a binding in scope. The Str module reads and builds them.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Foreign

Foreign

type

An externally owned pointer. The compiler never follows or releases it; the code that received it is responsible for it.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Handle

Handle

type

A counted owner with an external destructor, which runs when the last share is released.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Vec

(Vec a)

type

A growable vector of a. It owns its elements and is released at the end of its scope (MM-LIFE-2m). Build one with vecNew; Vec has the accessors.

Reference: reference.md#standard-library

Link

(Link a w)
(linkTo v i)  linkNone

type

An index into a (Vec a) that takes no share, stored in a struct field as w: UInt8, UInt16 or UInt32 (MM-VAL-10b). Make one with linkTo; Link has the accessors.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Option

(Option a)
(Some x)  None

type

A value that may be absent: (Some x) or None. Take it apart with match, writing the arms ((Some x) ...) and ((None) ...). Library functions answer it instead of a sentinel.

Reference: reference.md#standard-library

Result

(Result a e)
(Ok x)  (Err e)

type

Success or failure: (Ok x) or (Err e). The Err module declares it with Error, and a postfix ? unwraps one inside a function that answers a Result. A Result left unused in statement position is AX3046.

Reference: reference.md#standard-library

Addr

Addr

type

The identity of a heap value, from addrOf, for comparing values by identity and hashing them without a cast.

Reference: reference.md#standard-library

()

()
(:: log (-> String ()))

type

The unit type, and its one value. A function declared to answer () drops its body's value, an if without an else answers (), and a () branch or match arm makes the whole form answer (). Using a () where a value is wanted is a type error, so a dropped value can't be read by mistake.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

IO

;@axiom:effect(io)

effect

Reaches the outside world: a syscall, an extern call or the command line. It propagates through calls, so a function that performs IO without declaring ;@axiom:effect(io) is AX3042.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Alloc

;@axiom:effect(alloc)

effect

Allocates, resets the arena or installs a handler. Inferred through calls; effect(alloc) checks a claim and restrict(no-alloc) forbids it. Ordinary functions need not declare it. Generated retains and releases carry no separate reclamation effect.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Mut

;@axiom:effect(mut)

effect

Changes heap state that something else can see. Inferred through calls; effect(mut) checks a claim. Ordinary functions need not declare it. Reference-count bookkeeping does not add Mut.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Unsafe

;@axiom:effect(unsafe)

effect

Uses a raw-memory primitive, calls an extern or forges a reference. A function that does so must declare ;@axiom:effect(unsafe) (AX3073), which makes it a trusted wrapper; the effect does not propagate to callers. Its author must uphold address, layout and lifetime obligations for every well-typed call. Type, effect and restriction checks still apply.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Spawn

;@axiom:effect(spawn)

effect

Creates a task, thread or process.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Block

;@axiom:effect(block)

effect

Waits: a join, a lock, a read that may not return at once.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Entropy

;@axiom:effect(entropy)

effect

Draws randomness from the system or the hardware.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Div

;@axiom:effect(div)

effect

Possible divergence. Nothing infers it, so an effect(div) claim is refused with AX3110.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Pure

;@axiom:effect(pure)

effect

Performs no effect at all. Claim it with ;@axiom:effect(pure); a body that performs one is AX3010.

Reference: reference.md#effects

+

(:: + (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Arithmetic over two Ints or two Floats. Integer arithmetic wraps on overflow; floating-point arithmetic uses IEEE 754 binary64. Mixed numeric types require explicit conversion.

Reference: reference.md#operators

-

(:: - (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Arithmetic over two Ints or two Floats. Integer arithmetic wraps on overflow; floating-point arithmetic uses IEEE 754 binary64. Mixed numeric types require explicit conversion.

Reference: reference.md#operators

*

(:: * (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Arithmetic over two Ints or two Floats. Integer arithmetic wraps on overflow; floating-point arithmetic uses IEEE 754 binary64. Mixed numeric types require explicit conversion.

Reference: reference.md#operators

/

(:: / (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Integer division and remainder, truncating toward zero. Division by zero stops the program.

Reference: reference.md#operators

%

(:: % (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Integer division and remainder, truncating toward zero. Division by zero stops the program.

Reference: reference.md#operators

&

(:: & (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Bitwise and, or and exclusive or over two Ints.

Reference: reference.md#operators

|

(:: | (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Bitwise and, or and exclusive or over two Ints.

Reference: reference.md#operators

^

(:: ^ (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Bitwise and, or and exclusive or over two Ints.

Reference: reference.md#operators

<<

(:: << (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Shifts an Int left or right by a number of bits; the right shift is arithmetic.

Reference: reference.md#operators

>>

(:: >> (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Shifts an Int left or right by a number of bits; the right shift is arithmetic.

Reference: reference.md#operators

==

(:: == (-> Int Int Bool))

operator

Equality of two Ints. Strings compare with strEq, and heap values by identity with addrOf.

Reference: reference.md#operators

!=

(:: != (-> Int Int Bool))

operator

Equality of two Ints. Strings compare with strEq, and heap values by identity with addrOf.

Reference: reference.md#operators

<

(:: < (-> Int Int Bool))

operator

Compares two Ints and answers a Bool.

Reference: reference.md#operators

(:: > (-> Int Int Bool))

operator

Compares two Ints and answers a Bool.

(:: <= (-> Int Int Bool))

operator

Compares two Ints and answers a Bool.

AXTAG keys

;@axiom:effect

;@axiom:effect

AXTAG

Claims the one effect the function performs: io, unsafe or pure. The checker compares the claim with what the body does and refuses a mismatch (AX3010); a required effect left undeclared is AX3042. One effect per tag (AX3076), and purity is spelled effect(pure) (AX3078).

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:restrict

;@axiom:restrict

AXTAG

Claims what the function never does, transitively: no-alloc, no-io, no-unsafe, no-block, no-spawn, no-recursion, no-trap and the others. A violated claim is AX3049; add strict to refuse a claim the walk cannot prove instead of receiving AX3051.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:pre

;@axiom:pre

AXTAG

A precondition over the arguments, checked on every call. A failed check traps with status 80. A condition the compiler cannot compile into a check is AX3050.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:post

;@axiom:post

AXTAG

A postcondition over result, checked on every return. A failed check traps with status 80.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:isr

;@axiom:isr

AXTAG

Marks an interrupt entry point: a no-argument function checked for allocation, recursion and waiting. On baremetal-aarch64, isr(irq) binds the interrupt handler and isr(fault) the fault policy.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:ct

;@axiom:ct

AXTAG

Claims the function runs in constant time with respect to the named parameters, for code that handles secrets. A body that branches or indexes on one is refused (AX3092); a claim naming no parameter is AX3093.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:deprecated

;@axiom:deprecated

AXTAG

Marks a name as deprecated with a message. Each use draws AX3048 quoting it, and a release may retire the name under the compatibility rules.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:unhandled

;@axiom:unhandled

AXTAG

unhandled(trap) on an effect declaration says that an operation reaching main with no handler is intended to stop the program, which turns AX3053 off for it.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:syscall

;@axiom:syscall

AXTAG

Names the effects a raw syscall number performs, so every function that names the number owes them. The value is a comma list of effect names.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:nolint

;@axiom:nolint

AXTAG

Quiets hints and warnings, like Rust's #[allow]: a hint by name (lint-dead-branch, lint-bool-if, lint-unused-let, lint-axql), a warning by its code (AX3037), or a group (hints, warnings, all). On a declaration it covers that declaration; above an import it covers the whole file. It never quiets an error, and a name nothing answers to draws lint-unknown-nolint at the tag.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:result

;@axiom:result

AXTAG

result(owned) says the function's type-variable result carries a share the caller owns, so the caller releases it at scope end, after a call or when it is discarded, as vecPop's is. Accepted only beside effect(unsafe), since the checker cannot see a share transferred through a raw load (AX3116).

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:scoped

;@axiom:scoped

AXTAG

Requires the named callback to return a scalar and retain none of each invocation's reference arguments or fresh allocations in captured state. Pass a lambda directly, a non-nullary function declaration, or a parameter carrying the same contract. Call the tagged function directly with all declared arguments (AX3130). Escaping stores are AX3060; ordinary type and effect checks still apply. Raw reclamation remains the callee's unsafe obligation.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:compute

;@axiom:compute

AXTAG

Requires the named Int-to-Int callback to be a checked numeric computation (AX3131). It accepts canonical primitive captures, explicit conversions, numeric helpers and local accumulators. It rejects references, heap/raw stores, runtime observers, allocation, foreign/opaque calls and assembly, transitively. Forward only the exact parameter with the same contract. Local mutation retains its Mut effect; normal type and effect checks apply.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

Language index

Every word of the language: keywords, the words that are special inside a form, builtin types, effects, operators and literals, then the AXTAG keys. axiom explain WORD prints the same entry, and hover in your editor shows it.

Words

|>

(|> value (f args...) (g args...))

form

Passes a value through calls from left to right. Each stage receives the preceding result as its first argument; one direct _ places it elsewhere. Every intermediate result is evaluated once. Types, effects and region checks are the same as for ordinary calls.

Reference: reference.md#functions

fn

(fn (name param ...) body)

keyword

Declares a named function at the top level. Its type comes from the (:: name Type) signature above it, and AXTAGs such as ;@axiom:effect(io) go between the two. A function value inside an expression is a lambda; (fn (x) ...) there is refused with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#functions

lambda

(lambda (param ...) body)

keyword

An anonymous function. It captures the bindings it uses, can be passed as a value and may be applied to fewer arguments than it takes, answering another lambda. A lambda with no parameters is refused with AX3068.

Reference: reference.md#lambdas

let

(let name value)

keyword

Declares a local inside a { ... } block. The value is evaluated before the name enters scope; later statements can read it, and a later declaration can shadow it. Use (let mut name value) for a local that set can change. Destructure values with match. The block answers its last expression.

Reference: reference.md#let-bindings

set

(set slot value)

keyword

Overwrites a mut slot. The slot owns what it holds, so the previous value is released (MM-MUT-1). Writing to a binding that is not mut is AX3012.

Reference: reference.md#let-bindings

if

(if test then else)
(if test then)
(if t1 b1 t2 b2 ... else)

keyword

Branches on a Bool. Both branches must have the same type, unless one is (): then the if answers () and the other branch's value is dropped. Leave out the else and the if supplies (), so (if done (println "ok")) needs no filler. With more operands it is a chain: (if t1 b1 t2 b2 else) is (if t1 b1 (if t2 b2 else)). Use braces for a branch of several expressions.

Reference: reference.md#if

match

(match value (pattern body) ... (_ body))

keyword

Compares a value against patterns in order and runs the first body that fits. A pattern is a constructor with binders, a literal, a name or _. A match that misses a constructor is AX3005; a bare capitalised name such as None binds a variable rather than testing a tag, so write (None).

Reference: reference.md#pattern-matching

while

(while test body)

keyword

Repeats the body while the Bool test is true. There is no break or continue: put the stopping condition in the test. The form answers 0.

Reference: reference.md#while-loops

for

(for i in lo..hi body)
(for i in lo..hi by step body)
(for x in vec body)
(for (x i) in vec body)

keyword

Counts over a range, lo included and hi excluded, with an optional by step, or walks a Vec by element or by (x i) element and index. The sequence is evaluated once. A for body is for effects, and the form answers 0.

Reference: reference.md#for-loops

data

(data Name (Ctor Type ...) ...)
(data Name (a) (Ctor a) ...)

keyword

Declares a sum type: a set of constructors, each with zero or more field types. Constructors start with a capital, build values when applied and take values apart in match. Type parameters go in a list after the name.

Reference: reference.md#algebraic-data-types

struct

(struct Name (field : Type) ...)

keyword

Declares a product type with named, typed fields. Build one with named values, (Point :x 1 :y 2), and read a field with a dot, p.x. Supply each field exactly once. Values are evaluated in written order. A field declaration without its : is refused with AX3056.

Reference: reference.md#structs

type

(type Name Type)

keyword

Gives an existing type a second name. Declare parameters between the name and the target, (type Items a (Vec a)), and apply them in type position, (Items Int). Aliases expand transparently and must be finite.

Reference: reference.md#type-aliases

subtype

(subtype Name is Int range lo..hi)

keyword

Declares a range-constrained Int, (subtype Port is Int range 1..65536). A value is checked against the range when it enters the subtype, and a failed check stops the program with its own message.

Reference: reference.md#range-constrained-subtypes

effect

(effect Name (op :: Type) ...)

keyword

Declares an effect: a name and the operations it provides, each with a signature. A call to an operation runs the innermost handle for its effect. A declared effect cannot take a built-in effect's name (AX3054), and an operation needs a type (AX3055).

Reference: reference.md#effects

handle

(handle body (Effect ...) handler)

keyword

Runs a body with a handler installed for an effect's operations. The list names every effect the body performs: a declared effect is intercepted and a built-in one is acknowledged and still reaches the caller. The handler's return value is the operation's result.

Reference: reference.md#effects

region

(region r body)

keyword

Opens a named arena scope. Values allocated inside it are released together when the body ends, and a value that would leave it is refused (AX3059). The compiler infers reference origins through calls and refuses stores into older objects.

Reference: reference.md#regions

parallel

(parallel ((name expr) ...) body)

keyword

Evaluates its bindings at the same time, each on its own task, and runs the body once all of them have answered. A binding may capture a parent value only by borrowing it for the extent of the form (AX3064).

Reference: reference.md#concurrency

macro

(macro (name param ...) template)
(macro name ((name pattern ...) template) ...)

keyword

Declares a macro: a template substituted at its invocation before the type checker runs. The one-rule form names the parameters in the head; the multi-rule form lists patterns and a template for each, which is declarations or one expression, and where the macro is invoked picks which. Hygiene renames the binders a template introduces.

Reference: reference.md#macros

import

(import Module)
(import Module (name ...))

keyword

Brings a module's public names into scope, all of them or the ones listed. A module is a file in the standard library, on AXIOM_PATH or in a dependency. A name declared in two imported modules is AX3014 when used bare.

Reference: reference.md#modules-and-imports

pub

(pub :: name Type)
(pub fn (name ...) body)

keyword

Marks a declaration as public, so other modules can import it. A signature and its function are each marked. A name used from a module that does not export it is AX3023.

Reference: reference.md#modules-and-imports

extern

(extern "crate" (name :: Type (symbol "sym")) ...)

keyword

Binds functions from a Rust crate built by axiom fetch. Each item gives the Axiom type and the symbol it binds; a type that cannot cross the boundary is AX3036. Calling one is an Unsafe operation.

Reference: reference.md#calling-rust

syntax/for

(syntax/for (C (syntax/constructors T)) template)

keyword

Inside a macro template, repeats the template once for each element of a syntax query such as (syntax/constructors T), binding the pattern variable to each.

Reference: reference.md#macros

alloc

(alloc Type)          ; removed

keyword

Removed. The form typed as a pointer and evaluated to 0, so a program holding one held no memory. Allocate with a constructor, a struct or a library function; the compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

begin

(begin a b c)         ; removed: write { a b c }

keyword

Removed. Sequence expressions with a brace block, { a b c }, which answers its last expression. The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

cond

(cond (t1 b1) (t2 b2) else)   ; removed: write (if t1 b1 t2 b2 else)

keyword

Removed. Write the chain with if: (if t1 b1 t2 b2 else) nests as (if t1 b1 (if t2 b2 else)). The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

consume

(consume x)           ; removed

keyword

Removed. It was a parse-time marker that enforced nothing. Ownership follows the memory model's rules without it; the compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

define

(define (name ...) body)     ; removed: write (fn (name ...) body)

keyword

Removed. It was the old spelling of fn, and a language with two spellings of one thing makes every reader learn both. The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

union

(union Name ...)      ; removed: write (data Name ...)

keyword

Removed. An untagged union cannot be pattern-matched safely, since its variants are not distinguishable at run time. Use data; the compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

foreign

(foreign ...)         ; removed: write (extern ...)

keyword

Removed. Bind native code with extern, which names the crate and checks each item's type. The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

trait

(trait Name ...)  (impl Name for Type ...)   ; removed

keyword

Removed. Traits and impls are not part of the language; write the function you want, or derive one with a macro such as deriveEq. The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

impl

(trait Name ...)  (impl Name for Type ...)   ; removed

keyword

Removed. Traits and impls are not part of the language; write the function you want, or derive one with a macro such as deriveEq. The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

emacro

(emacro name rule ...)  ; removed: write (macro name rule ...)

keyword

Removed. It was the multi-rule form for expression templates; macro takes the same rules, (macro total ((total x) x) ((total x rest ...) (+ x (total rest ...)))). The compiler refuses the word with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

cast

(cast Type value)  ; removed: write (as value Type)

keyword

Removed. Write (as value Type), with the value before its target type. Numeric conversions change the number; reference conversions retain their checked ownership and unsafe obligations. The compiler refuses cast with AX2004.

Reference: reference.md#removed-features

mut

(let mut name value)

form

Marks a let binding as a slot that set can overwrite. The slot owns what it holds and releases what set replaces (MM-MUT-1).

Reference: reference.md#mutable-bindings

in

(for x in xs body)

form

Separates the loop variable of a for from the range or Vec it walks.

Reference: reference.md#for-loops

by

(for i in lo..hi by step body)

form

Gives a for over a range its stride. A negative stride counts down; a literal zero stride is refused.

Reference: reference.md#for-loops

is

(subtype Name is Int range lo..hi)

form

In a subtype, names the base type the new type refines.

Reference: reference.md#range-constrained-subtypes

range

(subtype Name is Int range lo..hi)

form

In a subtype, gives the inclusive bounds a value must satisfy.

Reference: reference.md#range-constrained-subtypes

::

(:: name Type)

form

A type signature. At the top level it declares the type of the function or constant below it, (:: bump (-> Int Int)). Inside an effect, it types an operation. Two signatures for one name are refused with AX3006.

Reference: reference.md#functions

->

(-> Arg ... Result)

form

A function type: the argument types, then the result. (-> Int String) takes an Int and answers a String; (-> a a) answers the type it takes.

Reference: reference.md#functions

..

lo..hi

form

A range, lo included and hi excluded in for, both included in a subtype's range.

Reference: reference.md#for-loops

?

(f x)?

form

Propagates a Result or an Option. In a function that answers a Result, (f x)? answers the Ok payload and an Err returns from the function. In a function that answers an Option, it answers the Some payload and None returns from the function. Nothing after the ? runs. This includes a branch, a let body, a loop, a region or a handler. A Result leaves a region only when its payload and its error are both scalars.

Reference: reference.md#propagate-an-error-with-

_

(match v (_ body))
(f _ 2)

form

The wildcard. In a pattern it matches anything and binds nothing. In a call, (f _ 2) builds a lambda over the missing arguments from left to right.

Reference: reference.md#partial-application

as

(as value Type)

form

Converts a value to the written type. Int and Float conversions operate on numeric values; floatToBits and floatFromBits reinterpret bits. A reference converted to a word, such as Int or Foreign, keeps no ownership share: keep the owner alive while using the word. For identity comparisons and hashing, use addrOf. Converting a word to a reference requires effect(unsafe), a valid representation and a live backing owner. A conversion never extends a region's scope.

Reference: reference.md#types

sizeof

(sizeof Type)

form

The size in bytes of a type's representation. Takes exactly one type (AX3069).

Reference: reference.md#types

alignof

(alignof Type)

form

The alignment in bytes of a type's representation. Takes exactly one type (AX3069).

Reference: reference.md#types

asm

(asm (ARCH "template" operand...) ...)

form

Inline assembly: one arm per architecture, each a template and its operands. A form the compiler cannot lower is AX3091, and a template line the assembler rejects is AX3117, reported at that line when the program is built. See the reference's inline assembly section for the operands and options.

Reference: reference.md#inline-assembly

syntax/join

(syntax/join prefix Name)

form

Inside a macro template, builds a name from parts: (syntax/join eq T) with T bound to Colour is eqColour.

Reference: reference.md#macros

syntax/binders

(syntax/binders Ctor x)

form

Inside a macro template, the binder list for a constructor's fields, so a pattern can take any constructor apart without knowing its arity.

Reference: reference.md#macros

syntax/constructors

(syntax/constructors Type)

form

Inside a macro template, the constructors of a data type, answered from the declaration list at expansion time.

Reference: reference.md#macros

syntax/arity

(syntax/arity Ctor)

form

Inside a macro template, how many fields a constructor carries, folded to a literal.

Reference: reference.md#macros

syntax/fields

(syntax/fields Struct)

form

Inside a macro template, the fields of a struct, each as a name and a type.

Reference: reference.md#macros

decl

(decl declaration ...)

form

Inside a declaration macro, splices the declarations it holds into the module.

Reference: reference.md#macros

Int

Int

type

A signed 64-bit integer. Arithmetic wraps. It is also the word a handle or an address is carried in at the raw-memory level, which is why a heap value returned where a signature says Int is refused (AX3004).

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Int8

Int8

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Int16

Int16

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Int32

Int32

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

UInt8

UInt8

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

UInt16

UInt16

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

UInt32

UInt32

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

UInt64

UInt64

type

A distinct fixed-width integer. Use (as value Type) to convert explicitly. Arithmetic wraps at its width; division by zero, signed division overflow and out-of-range shifts trap. Literals remain Int.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Float

Float

type

An IEEE 754 binary64 number. Convert explicitly with (as value Float) and (as value Int). Numeric types never widen or narrow implicitly. Use floatToBits and floatFromBits to reinterpret bits.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Bool

Bool

type

true or false. The test of if and while, and the result of the comparison and logical operators.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Char

Char

type

A Unicode code point. Utf8 and Str convert between characters and byte strings.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

String

String

type

A byte string. Literals support {name} holes that interpolate a binding in scope. The Str module reads and builds them.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Foreign

Foreign

type

An externally owned pointer. The compiler never follows or releases it; the code that received it is responsible for it.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Handle

Handle

type

A counted owner with an external destructor, which runs when the last share is released.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Vec

(Vec a)

type

A growable vector of a. It owns its elements and is released at the end of its scope (MM-LIFE-2m). Build one with vecNew; Vec has the accessors.

Reference: reference.md#standard-library

Link

(Link a w)
(linkTo v i)  linkNone

type

An index into a (Vec a) that takes no share, stored in a struct field as w: UInt8, UInt16 or UInt32 (MM-VAL-10b). Make one with linkTo; Link has the accessors.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

Option

(Option a)
(Some x)  None

type

A value that may be absent: (Some x) or None. Take it apart with match, writing the arms ((Some x) ...) and ((None) ...). Library functions answer it instead of a sentinel.

Reference: reference.md#standard-library

Result

(Result a e)
(Ok x)  (Err e)

type

Success or failure: (Ok x) or (Err e). The Err module declares it with Error, and a postfix ? unwraps one inside a function that answers a Result. A Result left unused in statement position is AX3046.

Reference: reference.md#standard-library

Addr

Addr

type

The identity of a heap value, from addrOf, for comparing values by identity and hashing them without a cast.

Reference: reference.md#standard-library

()

()
(:: log (-> String ()))

type

The unit type, and its one value. A function declared to answer () drops its body's value, an if without an else answers (), and a () branch or match arm makes the whole form answer (). Using a () where a value is wanted is a type error, so a dropped value can't be read by mistake.

Reference: reference.md#primitive-types

IO

;@axiom:effect(io)

effect

Reaches the outside world: a syscall, an extern call or the command line. It propagates through calls, so a function that performs IO without declaring ;@axiom:effect(io) is AX3042.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Alloc

;@axiom:effect(alloc)

effect

Allocates, resets the arena or installs a handler. Inferred through calls; effect(alloc) checks a claim and restrict(no-alloc) forbids it. Ordinary functions need not declare it. Generated retains and releases carry no separate reclamation effect.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Mut

;@axiom:effect(mut)

effect

Changes heap state that something else can see. Inferred through calls; effect(mut) checks a claim. Ordinary functions need not declare it. Reference-count bookkeeping does not add Mut.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Unsafe

;@axiom:effect(unsafe)

effect

Uses a raw-memory primitive, calls an extern or forges a reference. A function that does so must declare ;@axiom:effect(unsafe) (AX3073), which makes it a trusted wrapper; the effect does not propagate to callers. Its author must uphold address, layout and lifetime obligations for every well-typed call. Type, effect and restriction checks still apply.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Spawn

;@axiom:effect(spawn)

effect

Creates a task, thread or process.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Block

;@axiom:effect(block)

effect

Waits: a join, a lock, a read that may not return at once.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Entropy

;@axiom:effect(entropy)

effect

Draws randomness from the system or the hardware.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Div

;@axiom:effect(div)

effect

Possible divergence. Nothing infers it, so an effect(div) claim is refused with AX3110.

Reference: reference.md#effects

Pure

;@axiom:effect(pure)

effect

Performs no effect at all. Claim it with ;@axiom:effect(pure); a body that performs one is AX3010.

Reference: reference.md#effects

+

(:: + (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Arithmetic over two Ints or two Floats. Integer arithmetic wraps on overflow; floating-point arithmetic uses IEEE 754 binary64. Mixed numeric types require explicit conversion.

Reference: reference.md#operators

-

(:: - (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Arithmetic over two Ints or two Floats. Integer arithmetic wraps on overflow; floating-point arithmetic uses IEEE 754 binary64. Mixed numeric types require explicit conversion.

Reference: reference.md#operators

*

(:: * (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Arithmetic over two Ints or two Floats. Integer arithmetic wraps on overflow; floating-point arithmetic uses IEEE 754 binary64. Mixed numeric types require explicit conversion.

Reference: reference.md#operators

/

(:: / (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Integer division and remainder, truncating toward zero. Division by zero stops the program.

Reference: reference.md#operators

%

(:: % (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Integer division and remainder, truncating toward zero. Division by zero stops the program.

Reference: reference.md#operators

&

(:: & (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Bitwise and, or and exclusive or over two Ints.

Reference: reference.md#operators

|

(:: | (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Bitwise and, or and exclusive or over two Ints.

Reference: reference.md#operators

^

(:: ^ (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Bitwise and, or and exclusive or over two Ints.

Reference: reference.md#operators

<<

(:: << (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Shifts an Int left or right by a number of bits; the right shift is arithmetic.

Reference: reference.md#operators

>>

(:: >> (-> Int Int Int))

operator

Shifts an Int left or right by a number of bits; the right shift is arithmetic.

Reference: reference.md#operators

==

(:: == (-> Int Int Bool))

operator

Equality of two Ints. Strings compare with strEq, and heap values by identity with addrOf.

Reference: reference.md#operators

!=

(:: != (-> Int Int Bool))

operator

Equality of two Ints. Strings compare with strEq, and heap values by identity with addrOf.

Reference: reference.md#operators

<

(:: < (-> Int Int Bool))

operator

Compares two Ints and answers a Bool.

Reference: reference.md#operators

>

(:: > (-> Int Int Bool))

operator

Compares two Ints and answers a Bool.

Reference: reference.md#operators

<=

(:: <= (-> Int Int Bool))

operator

Compares two Ints and answers a Bool.

Reference: reference.md#operators

>=

(:: >= (-> Int Int Bool))

operator

Compares two Ints and answers a Bool.

Reference: reference.md#operators

&&

(:: && (-> Bool Bool Bool))

operator

Logical and, or over two Bools. Both operands are evaluated.

Reference: reference.md#operators

||

(:: || (-> Bool Bool Bool))

operator

Logical and, or over two Bools. Both operands are evaluated.

Reference: reference.md#operators

!

(:: ! (-> Bool Bool))

operator

Logical not.

Reference: reference.md#operators

true

(:: true Bool)

literal

A Bool literal. The two names are reserved: a binding or declaration called true or false is refused (AX3094).

Reference: reference.md#literals

false

(:: false Bool)

literal

A Bool literal. The two names are reserved: a binding or declaration called true or false is refused (AX3094).

AXTAG keys

;@axiom:effect

;@axiom:effect

AXTAG

Claims the one effect the function performs: io, unsafe or pure. The checker compares the claim with what the body does and refuses a mismatch (AX3010); a required effect left undeclared is AX3042. One effect per tag (AX3076), and purity is spelled effect(pure) (AX3078).

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:restrict

;@axiom:restrict

AXTAG

Claims what the function never does, transitively: no-alloc, no-io, no-unsafe, no-block, no-spawn, no-recursion, no-trap and the others. A violated claim is AX3049; add strict to refuse a claim the walk cannot prove instead of receiving AX3051.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:pre

;@axiom:pre

AXTAG

A precondition over the arguments, checked on every call. A failed check traps with status 80. A condition the compiler cannot compile into a check is AX3050.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:post

;@axiom:post

AXTAG

A postcondition over result, checked on every return. A failed check traps with status 80.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:isr

;@axiom:isr

AXTAG

Marks an interrupt entry point: a no-argument function checked for allocation, recursion and waiting. On baremetal-aarch64, isr(irq) binds the interrupt handler and isr(fault) the fault policy.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:ct

;@axiom:ct

AXTAG

Claims the function runs in constant time with respect to the named parameters, for code that handles secrets. A body that branches or indexes on one is refused (AX3092); a claim naming no parameter is AX3093.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:deprecated

;@axiom:deprecated

AXTAG

Marks a name as deprecated with a message. Each use draws AX3048 quoting it, and a release may retire the name under the compatibility rules.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:unhandled

;@axiom:unhandled

AXTAG

unhandled(trap) on an effect declaration says that an operation reaching main with no handler is intended to stop the program, which turns AX3053 off for it.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:syscall

;@axiom:syscall

AXTAG

Names the effects a raw syscall number performs, so every function that names the number owes them. The value is a comma list of effect names.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:nolint

;@axiom:nolint

AXTAG

Quiets hints and warnings, like Rust's #[allow]: a hint by name (lint-dead-branch, lint-bool-if, lint-unused-let, lint-axql), a warning by its code (AX3037), or a group (hints, warnings, all). On a declaration it covers that declaration; above an import it covers the whole file. It never quiets an error, and a name nothing answers to draws lint-unknown-nolint at the tag.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:result

;@axiom:result

AXTAG

result(owned) says the function's type-variable result carries a share the caller owns, so the caller releases it at scope end, after a call or when it is discarded, as vecPop's is. Accepted only beside effect(unsafe), since the checker cannot see a share transferred through a raw load (AX3116).

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:scoped

;@axiom:scoped

AXTAG

Requires the named callback to return a scalar and retain none of each invocation's reference arguments or fresh allocations in captured state. Pass a lambda directly, a non-nullary function declaration, or a parameter carrying the same contract. Call the tagged function directly with all declared arguments (AX3130). Escaping stores are AX3060; ordinary type and effect checks still apply. Raw reclamation remains the callee's unsafe obligation.

Reference: reference.md#axtag-metadata

;@axiom:compute

;@axiom:compute

AXTAG

Requires the named Int-to-Int callback to be a checked numeric computation (AX3131). It accepts canonical primitive captures, explicit conversions, numeric helpers and local accumulators. It rejects references, heap/raw stores, runtime observers, allocation, foreign/opaque calls and assembly, transitively. Forward only the exact parameter with the same contract. Local mutation retains its Mut effect; normal type and effect checks apply.
